newsitem.title: USA: Boeing '97 outlook remains same - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Boeing '97 outlook remains same - analyst.

text.p: The outlook for Boeing Co through the rest of 1997 remains mostly unchanged despite lower-than-expected first quarter results, an analyst said Monday.

"Analysts' expectations might have got ahead of where they should have been, but for the year ... things are no different from where they were three months ago," said Peter Jacobs, an analyst at Ragan MacKenzie in Seattle.

Shares in the airplane maker were down 5-5/8 to 96-3/8 in late-morning trade. They had opened down seven at 95 after the campany reported it earned $0.87 a share in the first quarter, below a consensus estimate by First Call of $1.
Jacobs said Boeing was hit partly by higher costs as it readied for boosting output and by research-and-development expenses for its new 737 and 757 airliners.
"You end up solving problems sometimes by throwing money at them," he said.
He said the company had warned of lower operating margins three or six months ago and his estimate of the company's 1997 earnings per share remained unchanged at $5 against $3.19 for 1996.
